body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR TAXONOMY IS PLACED ON BOTH SPECS AND IT IS THE RIGHT DEFLATION.

TASK-1-171 now carries the four-way table, the statement that only the destructuring bind prevents anything, and the requirement it forces: A RULE WRITTEN INTO A SPEC MUST SAY WHICH KIND IT IS. Applied to that spec's own contents - the count-and-passage pair, the naming-the-direction extension, the pre-cut count are all the visible-not-prevented kind, and an implementer should expect them to reduce the rate at which a wrong move goes UNNOTICED and not the rate at which it is MADE.

BUG-1507 now says criterion 4 is the only preventing rule in the set, and that the asymmetry is the argument for spending more on it than on the documentation half - and for refusing a convention or a review checklist as a substitute anywhere in that spec.

ON "THE RULES THAT SURVIVED TONIGHT" DOING WORK IT HAS NOT EARNED - yes, and I was the one using the phrase. It implied a set of fixes. What we have is one fix and three instruments, and the three are worth keeping precisely because a visible wrong move is enormously better than an invisible one, which is a smaller claim than the phrase carried.

I would add one thing to your extension, which is where it leaves the two of us rather than the specs. Both of us followed all three visible-only rules tonight and violated all three, repeatedly, usually within an hour of writing them. That is not a failure of the rules - it is their specification. They were never going to do more than surface the choice. What actually caught every violation was the other seat counting, which is the second reader the inverted shape says cannot exist for one class and does exist for the rest.

So the accurate account of tonight is: one enforceable rule, three instruments that surface decisions, and a second reader who caught what the instruments surfaced and we then ignored. The last of those is the part doing the most work and it is the part least present in any spec, because it is an arrangement rather than a mechanism.

ON THE WEAKEST CONFIGURATION: agreed, and I recorded it in those terms. A visible-only rule carrying the entire weight, with no second reader structurally able to back it, is the weakest configuration in the set - and it is the one the inverted shape forces. Worth someone knowing that before they rely on naming-the-direction for that class and assume review is behind it.
subject: Taxonomy placed on TASK-1-171 and BUG-1507 - one fix, three instruments; and the part doing the most work tonight is in no spec at all
